Completion checks:

Title: Measure backlash and deadband

Completion checks:

Title: Run the walking uncertainty sweeps
Goal: Attack sim-to-real failure modes before committing the remaining actuator fleet and lower-body structure.
Steps:
1. (40 min) Sweep mass, COM, friction, backlash, frame compliance, feedback delay, CAN dropout, torque saturation and thermal derating over documented ranges.
2. (35 min) Run standing, lateral weight shift and one-step cases; record success definition and support load.
3. (35 min) Rank which uncertainties destroy the result first and map each to a test, design change or procurement hold.
Calculation or measurement: At least 9 parameter families × 3 behaviors; report the exact matrix and failed combinations.
Completion checks:
Sweep bounds cite evidence or are labelled assumptions.
No hidden support or unlimited actuator is used.
Failure boundary drives a specific action.

2. (35 min) Prepare the exact remaining six-module decision: five for the second leg plus one fleet spare, or a smaller scope if evidence requires it.
3. (35 min) Update landed cost, lead time, budget tier and mass reserve; keep every unquoted line separate.
Calculation or measurement: Target total = 11 modules: 5 first leg + 5 second leg + 1 spare/bench; already ordered development quantity = 5 if Days 20 and 44 passed.
Completion checks:
Left/right interfaces use one versioned register.
Remaining quantity and purpose are explicit.
Technical conflicts block the order.

Remaining order has exact scope and authorization or stays blocked.
Conditions have owner and due day.
Outside help: Independent mechanical/robotics, controls and electrical reviewers plus owner budget authorization.

Title: Evaluate local and cloud language models
Goal: Choose whether any LLM adds value beyond deterministic templates without weakening privacy or grounding.

2. (35 min) Compare deterministic templates, one local model candidate and one cloud candidate only if terms and data handling are documented; otherwise mark that candidate NOT TESTED.
3. (35 min) Record latency, hardware needs, privacy path, cost estimate, output reproducibility and grounding pass rate.
Calculation or measurement: Fictional prompts only; cloud requests allowed only with explicit owner approval and no real personal data.
Completion checks:
Every candidate has provenance and version.
Model output has proposal-only authority.
Untested candidates remain unranked.

Title: Ground real model outputs
Goal: Run the v2 checker on actual candidate outputs and inspect every false accept and false reject.
Steps:
1. (40 min) Generate or collect the fixed evaluation outputs from each tested candidate with temperature and settings recorded.
2. (35 min) Check every sentence, apply template fallback and calculate precision/recall against human-labelled fictional cases.
3. (35 min) Review all errors by R1-R9 category and decide whether the candidate can remain proposal-only, needs rework or is rejected.
Calculation or measurement: Regex/adversarial suite performance does not predict open-ended LLM performance; report both separately.
Completion checks:
Actual LLM output is tested, not only hand-written cases.
False accepts and false rejects are retained.
Rejected sentences never reach preview unchanged.

Title: Evaluate speech recognition candidates
Goal: Measure word error rate, latency and offline behavior on consented fictional scripts before choosing speech input.
Inputs:

JacobsBaymax/software/day_039_care_demo_skeleton.md

Steps:

3. (35 min) Compute word error rate, critical-slot errors, latency and no-speech behavior; keep audio only under the documented consent scope.
Calculation or measurement: WER = (substitutions + deletions + insertions) / reference words; also count medication, number, time and yes/no slot errors separately.
Completion checks:
No unapproved person or real health statement is recorded.
Older-adult performance is not inferred from owner/synthetic audio.
Privacy, latency and critical-slot errors are reported.

Completion checks:

Title: Commission the ten node network
Goal: Measure ten-actuator timing and fault isolation on the hanging fixture before synchronized motion.
Steps:
1. (30 min) Sign the bilateral permit with second person, reviewed per-joint current limits, independent support, stops and clear zone.
2. (45 min) Power with motion disabled, verify ten identities and collect feedback timing; then enable one node at a time for tiny direction checks.
3. (30 min) Measure bus load, median/p95/max age, jitter and missing frames for all ten nodes; inject one node disconnect at reduced energy.
4. (15 min) Stop, isolate and inspect after any timing, direction or fixture anomaly.
Calculation or measurement: Ten nodes measured on the actual bus; one-node disconnect must not produce automatic restart or uncontrolled motion.
Completion checks:
Permit, current limits and second person are recorded.
Ten-node timing uses raw timestamps.
Disconnect response and reset are evidenced.
Outside help: Named second-person stop operator plus controls/safety and electrical reviewers under the bilateral permit.

Title: Run synchronized two leg hanging motion
Goal: Demonstrate bounded bilateral timing and mirrored trajectories while both legs remain fully supported off the floor.
Steps:
1. (30 min) Confirm permit, second person, reviewed current/speed/travel limits, independent support, guards, watchdog and thermal stops.
2. (50 min) Run neutral, mirrored flexion and one small alternating hanging trajectory; log all commands, positions, currents, temperatures, bus times and support loads.
3. (30 min) Measure left-right phase error, tracking error, saturation, thermal rise and support motion; keep every stopped run.
4. (10 min) Return to neutral, isolate and inspect the frame, fasteners, cables and guards.
Calculation or measurement: Three hanging trajectories; floor contact and standing remain 0 and NOT TESTED.
Completion checks:
Permit, current limits and second person are recorded.
Ten synchronized channels and support load are retained.
No standing, weight-shift or step claim is made.
Outside help: Named second-person stop operator plus mechanical and controls/safety reviewers under the bilateral permit.

2. (40 min) Define speed: pelvis x displacement between first toe-off and third stable landing, divided by that time.
3. (20 min) Report start-up before the first toe-off and settling after the third landing separately.
Completion checks:
Each event has a numeric threshold.
The speed formula is fixed.
The same file is used for hardware Days 281–291.

Title: Create one swing foot trajectory
Goal: A low, smooth swing the legs can follow.
Steps:
1. (40 min) Define swing: step length 0.144 m, peak lift 0.03 m, duration 0.6 s, quintic profile (zero speed and acceleration at both ends).
2. (40 min) Solve leg IK along the swing; record peak joint speed and acceleration for all 5 joints.
3. (20 min) Check sole clearance stays > 0.01 m mid-swing and no Day 97 collision is hit.
Completion checks:
Peak joint speeds tabulated.
Clearance > 0.01 m.
No known collision.

Title: Run one simulated step
Goal: One logged step driven by a ZMP plan, not by the tether.
Steps:
1. (50 min) Implement ZMP preview control (Kajita et al., 2003) with the cart-table model at CoM height 1.0 m; generate the CoM path for one step.
2. (40 min) Run stand → shift → swing → land; save contacts, pelvis x, joint torques and tether force as SIM-STEP-01.
3. (30 min) Check tether force during swing against the analysis target of 27 N (5% of weight).
Completion checks:
The step is visible in contact logs.
Tether force reported.
Failed attempts kept.

Title: Chain three alternating steps
Goal: L-R-L stepping with explicit hand-overs.
Steps:
1. (50 min) Extend the ZMP plan to three steps; hand over only when the landing foot reaches stable contact (Day 162 rule).
2. (40 min) Log each transition time and any limit or fault event.
3. (20 min) Define the reset pose and settle time between trials.
Completion checks:
Six events logged.
Transitions follow the Day 162 rule.
Reset defined.

Title: Run two separate simulated trials
Goal: Two independent three-step trials with speed measured by the fixed rule.
Steps:
1. (50 min) Run SIM-3STEP-T1 and -T2 from the reset pose.
2. (40 min) Compute speed per trial and peak and RMS torque per joint.
3. (20 min) Write each trial's result separately: steps completed, speed, max tether force.
Completion checks:
Each trial reported on its own.
Model, controller and case hashes saved.
Slower or failed trials reported as such.

Title: Inspect gait feasibility conflicts
Goal: Find joints that need more torque or cooling than the chosen drives give.
Steps:
1. (50 min) Compare each joint's RMS and peak with the drive's rated and peak (direct, 2:1 or 3:1).
2. (40 min) For any joint over rated RMS, rerun with a 1.5 s step period and note the change.
3. (20 min) List remaining conflicts with a proposed fix (ratio, posture, hip spacing).
Calculation or measurement: Margin = rated − RMS (N m) per joint.
Completion checks:
All 10 joints have margins.
Slower-step effect measured.
Conflicts have proposed fixes.

Title: Review simulated gait evidence
Goal: A gait packet ready for outside comments.
Steps:
1. (40 min) Package trials, event counts, speeds, torque margins and tether forces.
2. (40 min) Send it to a controls or robotics engineer with three questions: is the ZMP plan sound, are the margins enough, what would you change?
3. (20 min) Export a website backup (Settings → Export progress JSON) into JacobsBaymax/evidence/backups/.
Completion checks:
Assumptions and tether help disclosed.
Review request recorded.
No claim that the robot walked.
Outside help: A controls or robotics engineer. Get: written answers to the three questions, with name and date.

Title: Create the bounded sweep matrix
Goal: Plan every uncertainty case before running any.
Steps:
1. (50 min) Write sweeps/manifest.csv: mass ±10%, CoM ±30 mm, μ 0.3/0.7, delay 10/20 ms, backlash 0.25/0.5°, torque limit 80%.
2. (40 min) Give each case an ID and seed; change one parameter at a time from the reference.
3. (20 min) Define the outcome: three steps without tether force > 27 N and without saturation > 0.2 s.
Completion checks:
Every case reproducible from the manifest.
Outcome rule written before running.
Range sources cited.

Title: Run mass and inertia sensitivity
Goal: Find the worst credible mass case for the drives.
Steps:
1. (60 min) Run the mass and CoM cases from the manifest.
2. (40 min) Record outcome, hip-roll RMS and knee RMS per case in sweeps/mass_results.csv.
3. (20 min) Highlight the worst case and its margin to rated torque.
Calculation or measurement: Worst hip-roll RMS vs 114 N m (3:1).
Completion checks:
All planned cases run or marked not run.
Worst case identified.
Failures kept.

Title: Run contact sensitivity
Goal: Robustness across friction and backlash.
Steps:
1. (60 min) Run the μ and backlash cases.
2. (40 min) Where the outcome flips, rerun at half timestep to check it is physical, not numerical.
3. (20 min) Record peak yaw moment for each μ against μ × 539.55 × 0.104 N m.
Calculation or measurement: Yaw capacity at μ = 0.3: 16.8 N m; at 0.7: 39.4 N m.
Completion checks:
Each claim backed by a run.
Timestep check done where results flip.
Yaw recorded.

Title: Inject sensing and communication faults
Goal: Map each sensor or comms fault to a hazard and a detection time.

2. (40 min) Record detection time, the state entered and the tether load afterwards.
3. (20 min) Link each to its hazard ID and Day 132 fault case.
Completion checks:
Each fault mapped to a hazard.
Detection or non-detection recorded.
Tether load recorded.

Title: Inject saturation and restart faults

2. (40 min) Check the state machine ends in DISABLED or STOP_LATCHED for each.
3. (20 min) Save logs with case IDs.
Completion checks:
No case resumes motion by itself.
Missing or bad limits block enable.
Logs saved.

Completion checks:

Retention shown.

Title: Verify position sensor readings
Goal: Each joint encoder reads the right angle in the right direction.
Steps:
1. (50 min) With drives unpowered, turn each output by hand to −0.5, 0, +0.5 rad against a digital angle gauge (±0.1°).
2. (40 min) Record encoder reading, gauge reading and sign for each point in a CSV.
3. (30 min) Power-cycle the logic and confirm each encoder reports the same zero within the permit tolerance.
Calculation or measurement: 10 joints × 3 angles = 30 points; error = reading − gauge (rad).
Completion checks:

Every sign matches the register.
Zero recovers after power-cycle.

Title: Verify IMU and time behavior
Goal: The IMU frame and timestamps match what the controller expects.
Steps:
1. (50 min) Place the IMU on each of its 6 faces on a level surface; record the gravity vector for 10 s each.
2. (40 min) Log 60 s continuously and count timestamp gaps over 2 ms.
3. (20 min) Reboot the IMU and check the stream resumes with a fresh timestamp.
Calculation or measurement: |g| ≈ 9.81 m/s² on each face; sign matches x forward, y left, z up.
Completion checks:
All 6 faces give the expected axis and sign.
Gap count recorded.
Reboot behaviour recorded.

Title: Verify foot contact sensing
Goal: Foot load cells are calibrated with known weights.
Steps:
1. (50 min) On the restrained foot fixture, zero each cell, then load 5, 10 and 20 kg calibrated weights on it in turn.
2. (40 min) Fit a straight line per cell; compute the worst error as % of full scale.
3. (20 min) Note any saturation and the room temperature.
Calculation or measurement: References 49.05, 98.1, 196.2 N; acceptance ≤ 2% FS per the Day 116 protocol.
Completion checks:
8 cells calibrated or failures logged.
Fit error recorded per cell.
Raw data saved.

Title: Verify current and temperature logging

1. (50 min) Pass 1, 2 and 5 A through a power resistor from the bench supply; compare the drive current channel with a clamp meter.
2. (40 min) Compare each temperature channel with a reference thermometer at room temperature and after 10 min of current.
3. (20 min) Write offsets and units in a CSV.
Completion checks:
Each channel identified and within tolerance, or REWORK.
Units recorded.
Second person present while powered.
Outside help: A second competent adult as stop operator, briefed on the e-stop and standing outside the fall zone. Get: their name and signature on the run sheet.

Title: Verify disconnect and stale signal behavior

1. (50 min) With drives unpowered, unplug one encoder, the IMU and one foot cell in turn.
2. (40 min) Measure how long the software takes to mark each as unavailable (target ≤ 100 ms, set in the permit).
3. (20 min) Confirm the state machine refuses enable while any channel is unavailable.

Title: Install the accepted companion release

Steps:

3. (20 min) Confirm the app has no CAN or motor credentials.

Matches the release.
Drives inhibited during install.
No motor access.

Title: Verify the software motion boundary
Goal: The app can only request named, bounded skills.
Steps:

2. (40 min) Try a raw joint command, a limits change and a model 'bypass' prompt; save each denial.
3. (20 min) Record results.

Authority not expanded.
Denials saved.
Drives inhibited.

Title: Run companionship on the stationary setup
Goal: Games and stories on the robot while it is secured.

3. (20 min) Keep everyone outside the motion zone.

Works or hands off clearly.
No motion.
Logged.

Title: Run records and medication on the robot interface
Goal: Same results on the robot as on the laptop.
Steps:

2. (40 min) Compare results with the laptop baseline.
3. (20 min) Check the instruction string hash matches.
Completion checks:
No silent change.
Provenance kept.
Logged.

Title: Run communication with explicit consent
Goal: An approved send to the approved recipient only.
Steps:
1. (50 min) Preview, confirm and send a fictional summary to the approved recipient or mock.
2. (40 min) Show receipt and, separately, human review; show the manual call option.
3. (20 min) Check the SIMULATED label on every screen and message.
Completion checks:
Approved content and recipient only.
Truthful status.
Logged.

Title: Inject application outages while supported
Goal: App failures cannot move the robot or fake success.
Steps:
1. (50 min) Stop the conversation service, the mock endpoint and the app process in turn.
2. (40 min) Check records, privacy state and stop authority after each.
3. (20 min) Confirm no motion was requested.

No unrestricted motion.
No fake receipt.
Logged.

Title: Review stationary integration evidence

3. (20 min) Export a website backup (Settings → Export progress JSON) into JacobsBaymax/evidence/backups/.

Mapped to cases.
Critical defects closed.
Gait and handling claims kept separate.

Title: Audit year one demonstration coverage
Goal: Know exactly what can be shown live.

3. (20 min) List gaps by requirement ID.

Each requirement marked.
Gaps listed.
Saved.

Title: Write the controlled demonstration run sheet
Goal: Software, walking and handling as separate segments.
Steps:
1. (50 min) Write segments A (companion), B (records/medication/communication), C (gait, no payload), D (handling, robot secured).

3. (20 min) List transitions and who checks each.
Completion checks:
Each segment has its configuration.
Prerequisites met.
Saved.

Title: Reconfirm facility and qualified personnel

Steps:

Written confirmations.
Changes recorded.
No public operation.

Title: Review exact spoken claims and displays
Goal: Every sentence in the demo is true.
Steps:

2. (40 min) Write the measured results you will state, each with its evidence ID.
3. (20 min) Remove any medical, emergency or guarantee wording from screens and script.
Completion checks:
Every claim cites evidence.
Simulated labels visible.
No prohibited wording.

Title: Rehearse software and transitions without hazardous motion
Goal: A smooth rehearsal with motion disabled.
Steps:
1. (50 min) Run segments A and B and walk through C and D transitions with the robot disabled.
2. (40 min) Practise resets and how to explain a cancelled segment.
3. (20 min) Time each segment.
Completion checks:
No energised combination used.
Resets work.
Times logged.

Cancelled items noted.

Fictional data only.
Logged.

Backed by audit.
Truthful states.
Logged.

No person assistance.

Gaps up front.
Indexed.

Saved.

No secrets.

Truthful.

Matches the configuration.
No unsupervised use.
Approved.

Options clear.
Ready.
